increment: dev-environment correctness: derive DATABASE_URL from POSTGRES_*, and validate the Python interpreter by execution rather than by presence
evaluator: fresh independent reviewer; this is developer-environment infrastructure, not a ledger feature, so no passes flag is in play
approval_notes: Two dev-environment defects, one PR, both reproduced on ce2d58d BEFORE any fix. Neither is a product-behaviour change: apps/**, tests/** and .github/workflows/** are zero diff.

Defect A is worth fixing because its symptom misdirects: the stack dies with 'password authentication failed for user "atlas"' many frames down a SQLAlchemy traceback, which points at Postgres while the cause is in docker-compose.yml.

Defect B is NOT a broken CI gate. scripts/check-env.sh is not referenced by any workflow; it is referenced only by docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md and docs/CODEX_ENVIRONMENT.md. Its cost is that it is the documented first step a fresh agent session runs, so it currently certifies a Python that cannot execute code.
objective: A developer or agent who overrides only POSTGRES_USER / POSTGRES_PASSWORD / POSTGRES_DB gets a stack that comes up and passes smoke; and the environment scripts report Python honestly, failing loudly when no interpreter can actually run code.
scope: docker-compose.yml (api, worker, scheduler): the DATABASE_URL default is DERIVED via nested interpolation from ${POSTGRES_USER:-atlas}, ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-atlas} and ${POSTGRES_DB:-atlas}, matching the postgres service's own environment and healthcheck. A whole-string DATABASE_URL override still wins over every part.

scripts/check-env.sh, scripts/bootstrap-dev.sh, scripts/init.sh, scripts/smoke.sh: select a Python interpreter by trying python3, python, py in turn and accepting one ONLY when it evaluates a trivial program and prints a sentinel on stdout. Validation is on OUTPUT, not on presence and not on exit status. Pattern adopted from the already-merged _stack_python in scripts/stack-env.sh.
.env.example: DATABASE_URL is commented out so that copying the file to .env leaves derivation in force; the escape-hatch semantics and the URL-reserved-character caveat are documented.
docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md: replaces the note that told readers to set DATABASE_URL to match POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_DB (now false), and documents the execute-to-validate interpreter rule.
out_of_scope: apps/api/**, apps/web/**, tests/**, .github/workflows/**: zero diff, verified per path with git diff --numstat.
scripts/stack-env.sh, scripts/stack-env.ps1, scripts/stack-up.*, scripts/stack-smoke.*, scripts/stack-down.*, scripts/check_urls.py, scripts/url-allowlist.txt: zero diff.

agent-state/feature_list.json and agent-state/evaluation.json: zero diff. No passes flag is touched; this is infrastructure, not a ledger feature, following the precedent of the three preceding infrastructure slices.
The PowerShell siblings (check-env.ps1, bootstrap-dev.ps1, init.ps1, smoke.ps1) are NOT changed. They are reported as an observation, not fixed, to keep the diff reviewable.
No migration. No dependency change. No new service.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Overriding only POSTGRES_USER / POSTGRES_PASSWORD / POSTGRES_DB brings the full stack up healthy and passes stack-smoke. This is the case that fails on ce2d58d.
A2. A whole-string DATABASE_URL override still reaches api, worker and scheduler unchanged, including when POSTGRES_* are also set (DATABASE_URL wins).
A3. With no overrides the resolved values are byte-identical to ce2d58d: atlas/atlas/atlas against host postgres.
A4. All three services resolve the SAME URL, and the postgres healthcheck uses the same user and database. No unresolved brace survives interpolation.

B1. DECISIVE: with stubs first on PATH for ALL of python3, python and py, each printing the Microsoft Store advertisement and exiting 0 so exit status carries no signal, ce2d58d's check-env.sh reports ENVIRONMENT CHECK PASSED / exit 0 and the fixed script reports ENVIRONMENT CHECK FAILED / exit 1. Old and new MUST diverge; a control where they agree proves nothing.
B2. With the real interpreter available, check-env.sh reports a genuine version and exits 0.
B3. init.sh and smoke.sh stop claiming 'Agent-state JSON syntax: ok' when the interpreter validated nothing.

C1. Contamination: verification runs under COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=ftadbfix on API_PORT=8071 / WEB_PORT=8171, and the smoke result is shown to MOVE when only this project's API is stopped, proving the probe reached this stack and not another session's.
verification_plan: A-reproduction: ports-only .env -> stack healthy; then POSTGRES_USER/POSTGRES_DB/POSTGRES_PASSWORD overrides with the volume removed so Postgres initialises fresh -> quote the verbatim failure.
A-matrix: docker compose --env-file <case> config --format json for all four cases, decomposing the resolved URL into user/password/host/db per service and asserting brace count 0.
A-end-to-end: scripts/stack-up.sh then scripts/stack-smoke.sh with the overrides in force.

B-sabotage and B-positive as described in the acceptance criteria, comparing ce2d58d's scripts byte-for-byte (extracted with git show and length-verified) against the fixed scripts under one identical sabotaged PATH.
scripts/check.ps1 -NodeAudit: report exit code, PASS/FAIL counts, and the URL guard's URL and host counts.
Guardrail proof: git diff --numstat main -- <path> printed for every guarded path.
Cleanup: teardown scoped to COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=ftadbfix only; other sessions' stacks verified still running; probe .env deleted.
risks: Compose's support for ${} nested inside a default value is version-dependent. Mitigated by verifying the RESOLVED value with docker compose config --format json across all four cases rather than assuming the syntax parses as intended, and by recording the Compose version the evidence was gathered on.

Deriving the URL from parts means a password containing URL-reserved characters (@ : / ? # %) would corrupt the URL, where the previous hardcoded default could not. Mitigated by documenting the constraint in .env.example and docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md and by leaving the whole-string override available.
.env.example previously set DATABASE_URL explicitly, so anyone copying it to .env would have silently re-armed the defect. Mitigated by commenting the line out.

Behaviour change, intended and stated plainly: where no working interpreter exists, these scripts now FAIL where three of them previously reported success. On a machine whose only Python is a Store alias stub, check-env.sh goes from green to red. That is the point of the change, not a regression.
The interpreter helper is duplicated in four scripts rather than centralised, because each is a standalone entry point and the brief required their structure be preserved. Accepted and recorded.
Verification shares a Docker host with other sessions' stacks, one of which occupies 8000/8080. Mitigated by the ftadbfix project scoping and by the stop-my-API discrimination check.
required_evaluation_level: Level 1 - developer-environment infrastructure. No product code, no schema, no Z0 logic, no security boundary. Level 2 is not triggered.
contract_review: Written after reproducing both defects and BEFORE the fixes were committed, per the coding-agent instructions. Every measured claim in the ledger entry is marked as measured and separated from inference.
